deities: Lord Shiva as a patalaphuta Shivalinga in a circular yoni-pitha
Detached images of Chamunda, Surya, Buddha, Udyotasimha, four-armed Vishnu and Nandi in the precinct (mostly ruined)

history.dynasty: Eastern Ganga dynasty — built by 'Vishnu', a minister under Anangabhima Deva III (whose inscription survives in the temple)
history.summary: The Chateswar (Chateshwar) Mahadev Temple at Kishinapur village, near Paga-Gopinathpur in Salipur block, is an ancient Shaiva shrine housing a patalaphuta (self-manifested) Shivalinga within a circular yoni-pitha. On the evidence of detached sculptures of Saivite and Sakta affiliation (Chamunda, Surya, Buddha, Udyotasimha, Vishnu, Nandi) it is assigned to the Eastern Ganga period of the 12th century CE; the temple is pancharatha on plan with multi-segmented horizontal mouldings in the bada, in Kalinga style, and was built by a minister named 'Vishnu' under Ganga monarch Anangabhima Deva III, whose inscription is found in the temple. It is a living temple, managed by the Archaeological Survey of India (per lightuptemples), with heavy devotional crowds on Mondays and Sankranti days. CSV CORRECTION: the CSV town 'Cuttack' is the DISTRICT, too broad — the temple is at Kishinapur village (near Salipur), Cuttack district; 'Kishorenagar area' (task-brief guess) is not supported — sources say Kishinapur/Krishnapur. NOTE: a geocoder full-address match places a 'Chateswara Temple' at Choudwar (PIN 754028); Chatesvara also appears among the 'Asta-Sambhu' Shiva temples of Choudwar in scholarly sources — possible conflation of two same-named shrines; the Kishinapur/Salipur identification (Wikipedia coordinates, lightuptemples) is used here. Coordinates are from the Wikipedia infobox for this temple.

name: Chateswar Temple
town_description: Kishinapur (also spelled Kisinapur/Krishnapur) is a village near Paga-Gopinathpur in Salipur block, Cuttack district, Odisha, reached by road from Cuttack via Jagatpur. The temple is an ancient pilgrimage point in this rural stretch on the south-east coast of India.

travel.airport: Biju Patnaik International Airport, Bhubaneswar — nearest major airport.
travel.railway: Cuttack Junction — nearest major railway station (per lightuptemples).
travel.road: Easily accessed by road from Cuttack via Jagatpur to Kishinapur village; nearest bus stop at Kishinapur (per lightuptemples).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Maha Shivaratri, Dola Purnima and Kartik Purnima are the peak festival times.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Living temple drawing large crowds on Mondays and Sankranti days; exact daily darshan hours are not published online — verify locally before travel.
